dedupe_keys.name: crirsco international reporting template for exploration results mineral resources and mineral reserves

description: The International Reporting Template sets out how mining companies should publicly report exploration targets, exploration results, mineral resources and mineral reserves. It combines the minimum standards shared by national and regional reporting codes with recommendations and interpretive guidelines, sixteen standard definitions used identically or near-identically in members' codes, a checklist of assessment and reporting criteria and a guideline for technical studies. It is issued by the Committee for Mineral Reserves International Reporting Standards (CRIRSCO), whose members cover 16 countries and regions including Australasia, Brazil, Canada, Chile, China, Europe, India, South Africa and the USA, each with its own code such as JORC or PERC. The June 2024 update, which changed the standard definitions, is available to download free as a PDF, under CRIRSCO copyright; the template itself is not a mandatory standard. Caveats: it is a reporting framework, not data, and actual estimates appear in company filings under national codes that differ in detail. For simulation it defines the categories that separate proven and probable reserves from resources, which matter when mineral supply models and critical minerals scenarios draw on company reports for future production. It is related to the USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries record in this catalogue, which reports reserves by country.
